items.note: Figure 2.1: a monochrome leaf with the red minimum bounding rectangle drawn over it, the Rectangularity illustration. The label prints at the end of the parameter sentence ('... mention.lead_sentence: The greater the ratio of Circularity is, the closer the leaf is to a circle, (refer to figure 2.2)

mention.lead_sentence: The more this ratio is close to 1, the less jagged and the smoother this leaf’s contour is (refer to figure 2.3).

items.note: Figure 2.3: a monochrome lobed oak-like leaf with the red polygonal hull traced around its border, the edge-regularity illustration.

mention.lead_sentence: This time, the smaller this ratio is, the more jagged and irregular the contour of the leaf is (refer to figure 2.4).

items.note: Figure 2.4: a monochrome leaf inside a red bounding rectangle that is cut into stacked horizontal bands by red rules, the proportional-index illustration.

note: The paper numbers only four exhibits (Figures 2.1-2.4) and prints no table numbers, so the census counts measured blocks: 35 figure items and 20 table rows over 103 measured regions. Two named-but-unmeasured cases are left unresolved: the body text on p20 cites 'figure 3.1' for the leaf/tree pair although no caption prints that number, and the two table photographs on pp29-30 are headed inside the raster, so their printed numbers (if any) cannot be read from the text layer.
rules: Family follows the ink, not the page position: a block is photo-or-raster-image only where the crop is a photograph, so the four parameter illustrations keep that family even though each carries a drawn overlay [geometry.family].

Every hand-drawn construction - the sun-angle sketch, the two diamond outlines, the overlap-area construction, the growth-phase curves and the four-variable schema - is flowchart-or-schematic; only blocks with plotted tick numbers are line or scatter [geometry.family].

One measured raster can hold several panels: p9-r3 is a single 387x125 pt block carrying six numbered leaf photographs, recorded as composite-panel with panel_count 6 rather than as six rows [geometry.panel_count].

A photograph of a table is an exhibit but not a table: the three raster blocks on pp29, 30 and 39 have no measurable grid, so their family is table-as-figure and they carry a geometry block, not a table block [geometry.family].

Rule style is read off the grid itself: the comparison matrices print horizontal rules with a shaded header band, the formula tables box every cell, and p23-r4 draws no rules at all [table.rule_style].

Four printed tables have no header row on the measured block (the nomenclature table, the p10-r1 continuation, the p12-r1 grid and the p33-r1 continuation); header_rows stays at the schema minimum of 1 and the note states the fact instead of inventing a label [table.header_rows].

Only four exhibits in the paper carry a printed number, and each of those prints the bare label 'Figure 2.N' at the end of a parameter sentence rather than a separate caption line, so caption.verbatim is the label alone [caption.verbatim].
Uncaptioned exhibits still get an empty mention block rather than a borrowed citation: first_page stays null where the text layer never names the block [mention.first_page].
Section paths stop at the deepest extracted heading on the page, so the 5.2 and 5.3 pages carry only the chapter and subsection and the 7.3.2 pages stop at that subsection [place.section_path].

tables.note: symbol/definition pairs, one symbol column and one definition column, 24 data rows; the printed table has no header row (the first row starts with the symbol R), so header_rows is recorded as 1 and this note carries the fact instead of an invented header label. three data rows over six numbered columns: the numeric column labels 1-6 print in a shaded header band, the horizontal rules carry no verticals, and there is no word header or unit in the band.
